newsitem.title: INDIA: Moderate earthquake hits India-China border.
newsitem.headline: Moderate earthquake hits India-China border.

text.p: A moderate earthquake shook areas near the Indo-Chinese border on Thursday, but there were no immediate reports of damage or injuries, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
The news agency, quoting Indian Meterological Department (IMD) officials, said the earthquake, measuring 5.2 on the Richter scale, struck near the border at 4.57 a.m. (2327 GMT).
IMD officials could not be immediately reached for comment. On Tuesday, two moderate earthquakes shook Srinagar, the summer capital of India's northern Jammu and Kashmir state.
Earlier on the same day, an earthquake measuring 4.8 on the Richter scale, struck the northeastern state of Assam.
Late on Sunday, an earthquake also measuring 4.8 on the Richter scale struck the western state of Gujarat.
In 1993, a quake of 6.4 on the Richter scale devastated a large area of neighbouring Maharashtra state, killing more than 11,000 people, and leaving about 150,000 homeless.
Earthquakes between four and five on the Richter scale are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in populated areas.
